question: Should Claw bundles become a core lifecycle owner for globally shared MCP declarations and cleanup?
rationale: The PR introduces persistent core authority over executable and remote configuration while repository direction prefers bundle-style plugin ownership, and the governing RFC remains open.

options.title: Approve with safety gates
options.body: Accept Claw ownership after the RFC defines the distinct gap and the recovery, consent, trust, and coexistence contracts are complete.

options.title: Use plugin ownership
options.body: Package MCP declarations through bundle-style plugins and avoid adding a second core ownership ledger.

options.title: Defer pending RFC
options.body: Keep the draft open but do not merge this slice until the RFC and prerequisite stack are accepted.

recommendation.title: Use plugin ownership
recommendation.body: Package MCP declarations through bundle-style plugins and avoid adding a second core ownership ledger.

likelyOwner.reason: He is the strongest current-main history match for the shared MCP configuration surface affected by this ownership choice.
